questions.q: What does Group By fundamentally do?
options: Collapses rows that share the same value(s) in chosen column(s) into one summary row per group
Deletes duplicate rows without summarizing anything
Sorts the table by the grouped column
Splits one column into multiple columns
questions.explain: Group By combines many detail rows into fewer summary rows, one per unique combination of the grouping column(s), with aggregated values.

questions.q: In the Group By dialog, what's the difference between Basic and Advanced mode?
options: Advanced mode lets you group by more than one column and add multiple aggregations
Basic mode is only for numeric columns
Advanced mode is required for every Group By operation
There is no functional difference
questions.explain: Basic mode groups by a single column with one aggregation. Advanced mode adds "Add grouping" and "Add aggregation" buttons, letting you group by multiple columns and compute multiple summary columns at once.

questions.q: Which operation would you choose to find the largest single value within each group?
options: Max
Sum
Count Distinct Values
Average
questions.explain: Max returns the largest value found in that column within each group — Sum adds them all, Average finds the mean, and Count Distinct Values counts unique values.

questions.q: What does the "All Rows" row-level operation do?
options: Bundles every original row for that group into a nested table you can dig back into later
Deletes all rows in the group
Is identical to the Sum operation
Only works when grouping by exactly one column
questions.explain: Unlike column operations that produce a single summary value, All Rows keeps the full set of original rows for each group, nested as a table value, for further processing later.

questions.q: Twelve detail rows are grouped by Country and Sales Channel. How many summary rows result?
options: One row per unique Country + Sales Channel combination that existed in the data
Always exactly twelve rows
Always exactly one row
One row per country only, ignoring Sales Channel
questions.explain: Grouping by multiple columns produces one row per unique combination of those columns' values — in the lesson's example, six combinations produced six summary rows.
